parsed.answer:
This has been reported before, and I found no fix in the archive. Dragging a tab crashes the whole Terminal window, which kills every session in it. #18719 is the report you cite. It was closed as stale after the reporter was asked for a crash dump and no further activity followed, so it was not resolved. #18561 and #15689 describe the same crash. The crash is a stowed exception (0xc000027b) in Windows.UI.Xaml.dll, raised from the tab-drag pointer input. What the tickets suggest:
1. Enable automatic crash-dump capture, as described on the Terminal wiki's Troubleshooting Tips page. Reproduce the crash, then send the dump to the maintainers ([user] or [user]) and @ them in the ticket. Dumps contain buffer contents, so don't post them publicly. Also include the Event Viewer Application Error entry (Event ID 1000).
2. Try Terminal Preview. A maintainer in #18561 thought the 1.23 process-model changes might have fixed this. Your report on 1.24 shows it may still happen.
3. Check whether security or endpoint software is involved. BeyondTrust was suspected in #18561 and #15689. Also check whether Terminal is running elevated, since dragging tabs from an elevated window is a separate known problem (#4583, #4706).
4. In #15689, a portable zip build did not crash but the installed msixbundle build did. Trying the portable zip build is a possible workaround.
Until this is fixed, avoid dragging tabs, and use the tab context menu or keyboard shortcuts to move them instead.
